latest.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
latest.summary: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). latest.title: Counting quaternion extensions by multi-heights
latest.summary: We prove a case of a conjecture of Gundlach on the number of Galois extensions over $\QQ$ with bounded multi-invariants for the group $G=Q_8$. We also obtain results when imposing local conditions at the wildly ramified place. As an application, we prove asymptotics for the number of $Q_8$-extensions with bounded product of ramified primes.

latest.title: Experimental Benchmarking of a 256-Qubit Room-Temperature NV-Diamond Quantum Processor with an Optically Programmable Biomolecular Quantum Bus
latest.summary: We report Zeus-256, a room-temperature nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond processor with 256 simultaneously active processor-level logical qubits arranged in a 16 x 16 array. Each logical qubit combines an NV electron-spin ensemble with nuclear-spin memory and ancillary resources. latest.title: From the Bazaar to the Algorithm: AI as a Technology Friend, Not a Human Friend
latest.summary: This paper explores the philosophical and architectural implications of artificial intelligence, arguing that AI should be understood as a historical continuation of tools rather than an independent agent. Focusing on the core concept of the "technology friend," the study examines the dangers of profit-driven design choices that simulate human relationships, foster emotional dependency, and obscure responsibility. It proposes alternative frameworks, such as structural boundaries, non-deceptive interface design, and bridging mechanisms to human communities, offering a perspective at the intersection of the philosophy of technology, AI ethics, and cognitive science.

latest.summary: Many pathogens spend a substantial portion of their life cycle outside the host tissues. These two latter stages are critical for survival, dispersal and host encounter. However, the extent of intraspecific variation during these phases remains poorly explored, and it is still unknown whether they are organized into phenotypic syndromes contributing to infection success. items.summary: arXiv:2604.21861v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parametrically driven oscillators exhibit distinct dynamical regimes that strongly influence their computational capability as physical reservoirs. items.summary: arXiv:2610.12471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Satellite onboard computing faces an irreducible tension: mission intelligence requirements grow monotonically while power, mass, and radiation budgets remain fixed. This paper advances the state of the art on three fronts. First, we develop a formal mathematical model of spiking neural computation for satellite workloads, deriving closed-form expressions for energy consumption as a function of network sparsity, firing rate, and synaptic fan-out. items.title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Earth observation (EO) models are still built by hand. For each new task, experts design a training recipe and tune it against a benchmark. We show that this loop can be handed to an agent. Any verifiable task can be cast as a harness and a verifier, where the harness defines what the agent may use and the verifier defines what counts as success. Every EO task can be made verifiable, through labeled benchmarks, independent sensors, physical models or the repeated observation of the same place. Given only these two components, a general-purpose coding agent builds the EO model and improves it recursively on its own outputs. items.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Robots are increasingly autonomous in task execution, yet their improvement remains largely human-driven. This study investigates Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), in which physical experience guides lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its improvement procedure, making subsequent improvement more effective across tasks. Physical RSI faces challenges from noisy observations, continuous dynamics, costly trials, and irreversible consequences. We present an L0-L5 framework that differentiates capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, reserving L5 for independently verified recursive gain. items.title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
items.summary: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. Our 3D foundation model, anatomix, is used to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent…

items.title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
items.summary: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics, together with the recipe that produces it: (1) a shared anatomical action space that describes 20 robot families, from bimanual arms to dexterous humanoids, in common joint coordinates; (2) joint training on these families in visual, action-conditioned and world-action modes; and (3)…

items.title: Code-Switching Detection via Language-Selective Dimensions in Speech Foundation Models
items.summary: Code-switching (CS), the alternation between languages within an utterance, is common in multilingual speech but underrepresented in pretraining corpora. Increasing CS coverage requires finding relevant utterances in large speech collections so that they can be included in training data. One way to find such utterances is to transcribe the speech and detect language alternation in the text, but this depends on obtaining accurate multilingual transcriptions. We propose a lightweight method that detects CS directly from speech. items.title: Imaginary HTEE: Probing Criticality and Coherence
items.summary: We study the imaginary part of the holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE) in a charged asymptotically AdS$_5$ black-hole background whose dual field theory exhibits a critical point in the presence of a chemical potential $μ$ and temperature $T$. Identifying the imaginary part of the HTEE with the imaginary part of the pseudoentropy, we derive an analytical expression for this quantity and investigate its behavior on the stable and unstable thermodynamic branches. items.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with metric and multi-view relationships that remain implicit in RGB observations. Geometry foundation models recover this structure from RGB, but existing methods either fuse the estimated features with visual tokens and learn to use them from question answering alone, or align VLM latents with geometry features. Capturing geometry, however, does not ensure its use: zeroing the aligned latents of a released feature-alignment model leaves its accuracy unchanged. We introduce GeoReader, a framework that learns geometric representations for the VLM that reads them. First, we train lightweight Geometric Readers to produce continuous input tokens,…

items.title: Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction through LoRA Federated Training
items.summary: In Intelligent Transport Systems, protecting vulnerable road users, specifically pedestrians, is a paramount challenge. The present work contributes to this field, putting forth a distributed architecture in which vehicles connected to the cellular infrastructure collect pedestrians' trajectories and fine-tune a foundation model for pedestrian trajectory forecasting via federated training. A server positioned at the edge of the cellular network is responsible for aggregating the local model's parameters from the vehicles and updating the global model's parameters. items.title: MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain, A Multi-Sensor, Multi-Temporal Pretraining Dataset for Earth Observation
items.summary: Pretraining generalist Earth observation foundation models requires data that combine several sensors, varied temporal sampling and, increasingly, text, yet open datasets rarely provide all three in one consistent, easily accessible form. We introduce MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain, a collection of 279,166 tiles of 10 km drawn from the Major-TOM grid by clustering AlphaEarth embeddings. Each tile stacks Sentinel-2 L1C, Landsat-8/9, Sentinel-1 RTC, Copernicus DEM and ESA WorldCover on a shared 1056x1056-pixel, 10 m grid, complemented by cloud masks, OpenStreetMap entities and ERA5 weather. items.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. The inherited…

items.title: GeoMER: A Joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic Geometry Framework for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
items.summary: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) aims to understand human emotions by integrating information from multiple modalities such as speech and text. Psychological studies suggest that emotions exhibit latent hierarchical structured relationships in their semantic representations. However, most MER approaches rely on Euclidean representations, which capture fine-grained cross-modal interactions but do not explicitly provide a geometric prior for organizing hierarchical emotional structures. To mitigate this gap, we propose GeoMER, a joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic modeling framework that introduces hyperbolic emotion-core routing to capture higher-level, abstract emotional representations for…

items.title: Beyond the Encoder: Object-Centric Representations Emerging from Segmentation Foundation Models
items.summary: Foundation models are increasingly used as feature extractors for downstream tasks with limited data, typically through representations obtained from their encoders. However, foundation models trained for structured tasks such as segmentation also form object-specific representations during task execution, whose transferability remains largely unexplored. We investigate Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) object pointers, compact object-level representations produced through the segmentation pathway, as transferable representations for downstream tumour prediction. items.title: The Smart Buildings Challenge: Learning Foundation Models for Real-World Optimization at Scale
items.summary: Buildings cause nearly 40\% of carbon emissions in the US. Of total building emissions, HVAC systems are responsible for approximately 40-60\% and account for 15\% of global energy consumption. Despite advances in artificial intelligence, most buildings still operate as inefficiently as they did decades ago. Building optimization, perhaps more so than any other optimization problem, has enormous potential for Machine Learning (ML) driven impact on climate change, in both the short and long term. items.title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion
items.summary: Automating AI research creates a positive feedback loop between software capability and research effort. We study a stochastic realisation of this loop in which independent, positive, multiplicative improvements arrive at a rate proportional to a power of current capability. Within this model, randomness leaves the deterministic explosion threshold unchanged but replaces the blow-up date by an explicit distribution. items.title: Curvature measures and volume preserving flows in h-convex geometry
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce a concept of modified curvature measures for h-convex domains in hyperbolic space and prove a shifted version of the generalized Alexandrov theorem, which characterizes geodesic balls in hyperbolic space via modified curvature measures. This result generalizes the classical work of Kohlmann (1998). We further investigate a volume-preserving shifted $α$-Gauss curvature flow for strictly h-convex hypersurfaces in hyperbolic space and prove that for any $α>0$ the solution exists for all time and converges smoothly to a geodesic sphere. items.summary: We introduce \textbf{ABot Embodied Reasoning (ABot-ER)}, a unified embodied reasoning foundation model that breaks the tension between breadth and depth in embodied reasoning. Embodied intelligence demands the joint mastery of perception, planning, and execution, yet reconciling generality with specialization across this spectrum remains an open challenge. Within a single unified model, ABot-ER commands specialist-level depth across all three competencies, spanning spatial, scene, and temporal reasoning in perception; long-horizon action organization in planning; and point grounding and affordance in execution. items.summary: We study a massive scalar field in flat spacetime written in a time-dependent accelerated frame whose fixed-coordinate observers have maximal proper acceleration at $t=0$ and become asymptotically inertial without forming a horizon. items.title: Preliminary Exploration of Large Models Based on Self-Supervised Learning for Health Monitoring of Power Electronic Converters
items.summary: Current artificial intelligence (AI) methods for power electronics converters make limited use of the abundant unlabeled data generated during real-world operation. This underexplored resource holds significant potential for advancing model performance. To address this gap, this paper presents PE-TSFM, a time-series foundation model tailored for power module health monitoring. The model adopts the PatchTST architecture combined with self-supervised learning and is trained on more than 143 million timestamps, where over 98\% of this training data is unlabeled and collected directly from an operating traction converter. items.title: AReaL-RSI: Adaptive Scaling and Coordination of Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Scaling recursive self-improvement requires additional computation to produce useful research progress in reaching persistent objectives. Intuitively, more researcher agents can explore more hypotheses, but early evaluation scores might misrepresent their promise, shared findings could lose their applicability conditions, and useful procedures could remain confined to completed investigations. In this paper, we present AReaL-RSI, a framework for organizing a persistent research team of agents without updating backbone LLM weights. items.title: LensErase: A Foundation Model for Erase Anything
items.summary: We introduce LensErase, a general-purpose mask-based Erase Anything foundation model designed to cover a broad spectrum of real-world erase scenarios. LensErase supports diverse objects, visual text, watermarks, associated visual effects, multiple-object removal, and a wide range of object scales, aspect ratios, and image resolutions. First, to enable such broad coverage, we construct LensErase-100M, a large-scale dataset containing 101.07 million paired source-mask-target examples spanning diverse erase scenarios. Second, we pretrain LensErase from the text-to-image model Lens, adapting its strong generative prior to mask-based erasing. To efficiently incorporate the source image and…

items.summary: Generalizable AI-generated image (AIGI) and deepfake detection remain challenging due to the asymmetry phenomenon, where adaptation to limited training distributions can degrade the transferable representations of Vision Foundation Models (VFMs). Recent subspace adaptation methods mitigate this issue by freezing high-magnitude principal components while adapting the residual subspace. However, such magnitude-based decomposition is data-agnostic and does not explicitly account for target-relevant semantics, potentially leading to semantic misalignment. items.summary: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) enable diverse whole-body control, but adapting a pretrained controller to a new embodiment remains challenging because of kinematic and dynamic mismatch. We present TRACE, a framework for efficient cross-embodiment adaptation that preserves pretrained motion representations while specializing feedback control to the target robot.TRACE first injects kinematic priors into input and output projection layers and aligns nominal joint dynamics to reduce embodiment mismatch and support stable fine-tuning. items.title: Saliency-Guided Replay for Continual Learning in Deep Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are promising for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing, but they still suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning tasks sequentially. This work investigates the integration of Experience Packing and Replay (EPR) as a memory-efficient continual learning strategy for deep SNNs under low-latency constraints. The proposed framework combines Batch Normalization Through Time stabilized VGG9 SNNs with Spike Activation Maps (SAM), which provide forward-only explanations based on spike activity. items.title: dMRI-F: A Foundation Model for Generalizable Diffusion MRI Analysis from Sparse Acquisitions
items.summary: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) probes water diffusion within the brain, providing unique information about tissue microstructure and white matter connectivity. High-quality dMRI enables advanced and accurate analyses but demands dense acquisitions, resulting in long scan times and hardware constraints that are often infeasible. Further, dMRI requires dedicated computational methods to support diverse analysis tasks (e.g., parcellation, registration, and synthesis) for both neuroscientific and clinical applications. items.title: Information-based Unified Design Framework for NMR Magnetic Tracking System
items.summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) magnetic tracking offers a promising alternative to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based localization for medical robotic guidance. However, scalar field measurements and field-aligned marker moments constrain position and orientation tracking, requiring careful configuration design. We present a unified information-based framework that uses local covariance analysis to evaluate receiver geometry, marker separation, and external source configuration in on/off-board NMR tracking. items.title: RT-J: Large-Scale Pretraining of Relational Transformers for Context-Efficient Predictions

items.title: Beyond the Superintelligent Machine: A Systems Definition of Superintelligence for the Era of Agentic AI
items.summary: Superintelligence is usually defined as a machine intellect that exceeds human cognition across most domains. That framing conflates three distinct properties: computational capability, warranted knowledge, and legitimate authority. This article develops a systems definition suited to large language models, tool-using agents, databases, theorem provers, and other computational knowledge artifacts. Using conceptual synthesis and constructive requirement derivation, we distinguish a computational artifact, an operational self that preserves commitments and consequence history, and a normative principal that holds purpose and accountability. items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry explains many structural features of real-world networks, yet existing hyperbolic generative network models with community organization such as the nonuniform popularity-similarity optimization (nPSO) are restricted to unipartite graphs. Here we introduce a bipartite extension of the nPSO model called nBPSO, motivated by the prevalence of community organization in real-world bipartite networks and the emerging evidence of hyperbolic hierarchical connectivity in trained sparse neural networks. nBPSO provides explicit control over link density, degree distribution, average clustering, and community organization. items.summary: We study the geometry of the Poincaré ball equipped with a rotationally symmetric metric \(g_\eta\) conformally close to the hyperbolic metric \(g_{\mathbb{H}}\), with curvature pinched in \([-1-\eta, -1+\eta]\). items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agent not only to acquire new knowledge and capabilities, but also to reason about which existing capabilities remain valid, when they should be routed, tested, retained, deprecated, restructured, or replaced, and whether the mechanisms governing these decisions should themselves be modified. items.summary: 3D instance segmentation requires fine-grained geometric discrimination together with an effective representation of the hierarchical organization of real-world objects and scenes. Conventional transformer architectures, however, operate predominantly in Euclidean space, whose polynomial volume growth can be poorly matched to strongly tree-like structures and can contribute to feature crowding in cluttered scenes. items.title: Beyond Linear Causality: The Cosmological Uroboros Framework (CUF) as a Conceptual Ontological Schema
items.summary: This paper introduces the Uroboros Ontology, a conceptual, metalevel ontological framework that conceptualizes existence not as a linear temporal progression, but as a timeless, recursive causal loop. items.title: HyperCLIP++: Fine-Tuning CLIP for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Hyperbolic Space.
items.summary: CLIP, a foundational vision-language model, has emerged as a powerful tool for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation. items.title: Neural state reduction: a quantum-inspired framework for how latent conscious thought becomes reportable.
items.summary: Human conscious thought often appears as a diffuse, unstable, and only partly verbalizable field until attention, questioning, decision, or speech stabilizes it into a reportable form.
